niche: a Melbourne residential owners corporation's 2027 electrification works: which of its apartment risers need re-phasing or a larger rising main before the approved EV chargers and induction cooktop conversions are energised, each riser's busiest phase built from its apartments' July 2026 evening demand on the phase each single-phase supply is wired to, a link no register holds and the embedded network meters' hourly voltages resolve
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the embedded network's July 2026 interval data to the risers through the lot schedule, adds every approved charger and cooktop conversion at the standard's after-diversity demand and, finding no record of the phase any apartment is wired to, carries each single-phase apartment as balanced over the three phases, the planning convention for unknown phasing, puts every riser's busiest phase at a third of its total and designates only the risers whose total is over the line, missing the risers whose apartments bunch on one phase.
domain_test: General statistics, so the swap is of the method: the deciding quantity is each riser's busiest-phase demand, a data-integration estimate built on a link between every apartment's meter record and the phase it draws from, which no key or register provides and which the records themselves resolve because meters sharing a phase move together hour by hour; replacing that link with the balanced allocation, an installer's rotation or a simulated chance of bunching (generic summaries) changes the designated risers.

meters keyed by lot number while the switchboard schedule and the applications use apartment numbers (the plan of subdivision schedule is the crosswalk)

the rising-main ratings in a scanned PDF switchboard schedule table
a few three-phase penthouse supplies among the single-phase apartments

world.org_type: owners corporation of a residential strata complex that owns its embedded electricity network

driver: The decisive quantity is the peak of the busiest of each parent unit's three sub-groups, every member drawing on exactly one sub-group that no record names; members on one sub-group share that sub-group's swings, so each member's sub-group is read from how its own measured level moves with the other members' over the week, and spreading each member's draw evenly over the three, assigning members in the installer's rotation or pricing the chance of a bunching by simulation each misses the parents whose members bunch on one sub-group, which breach the per-sub-group limit while their total stays inside three times it.
driver_concrete: Each riser's 2027 busiest phase is its apartments' July 2026 weekday evening demand on that phase plus the approved chargers and cooktop conversions of the apartments on it, and a riser goes in the works package when that phase exceeds 80 per cent of the rising main's per-phase rating; no register records which phase an apartment's single-phase supply is wired to, the balanced allocation of the engineers' planning convention puts every riser's busiest phase at a third of its total, and the embedded network meters' hourly voltages, which sag together for the apartments sharing a phase whenever any of them draws, sort each riser's apartments into its three phases and show the risers whose apartments bunch on one phase.
stump: A competent analyst conforms the interval data, adds the approved loads at the standard's diversity and carries every apartment balanced across the phases because no record gives its phase, designating only the risers whose total is over three times the per-phase line; the step that lands it there is the balanced allocation, when each apartment draws on one phase and the meters' voltages show which.

differentiation.task147: 147 loses requests whose run of consecutive units crosses a full one; here nothing is lost or queued: a per-phase rating binds and the decisive step reads which of three phases each member draws on from how the members' voltages move together
differentiation.task159: 159 builds a backlog from services arriving with too little room; here there is no queue or backlog: the busiest of three fixed sub-groups breaches its own limit, and the step recovers each member's unrecorded sub-group from co-movement
differentiation.task270: 270 v10 credits free servers with the reach of where they actually stood from a location record; here nothing moves: each apartment is fixed on one phase that no record names, read from voltage co-movement, not from a location log

lineage.driver: A trailing four-period total at a cut-off runs only over periods whose year is closed by an annual filing on record at that cut-off, each period in the year its own record names, and only units holding a contract in force on the cut-off day are scored; a unit's contract can lapse between terms while the register still carries it from its first start to the renewed term's end, and because no unit was ever between terms at a published cut-off, scope read from the register's dates reproduces every published result, but at the first cut-off that finds a unit between terms that scope scores it on a true fall, offers it and re-splits the fixed pool with it in.
lineage.stump: A competent solver rebuilds the screen as held at the 30 September census, collapses the dual-grant returns, builds each grantee's twelve months from the identity on the register as held with every quarter in the year its own return runs within, gives back all 821 published rows, every offer and every rate, reads rule 4.1 against rule 2's census list and drops the 17 grantees whose year to 31 March 2026 has no annual return on the register, and strikes the offers at 34.79 cents on 10 names, because it takes scope from the grants register's start and end dates (start of the grant, end of its current term), which keep Ilam After School Care Society in, so it scores its true 13.62 per cent fall over the twelve months to June 2026 and offers it, when the Variations sheet shows that its term ended on 31 July 2026 and its renewal runs from 1 November 2026, nothing paid for August to October, so it held no operating grant in force at the census (rule 3.1), and the answer scores 132 grantees and strikes 42.55 cents on nine.

lineage.niche: calendarizing three gas utilities' cycle-read and bimonthly-read residential sales into the calendar-month county series a heating assistance administrator files under the state's energy data standard, which sets the 2026-27 grant split
lineage.driver: A total each unit records over its own reading interval, one period or two long, is split onto fixed calendar periods by how fast it ran inside the interval, which a sample of units measured every day shows running well below the neighbouring periods' rate early in one period and far above it late in the same period, so splitting by elapsed days gives that period its neighbours' average rate and misallocates every straddling interval by where its reading dates fall, while scaling the daily-measured sample up instead carries its members' smaller size.
lineage.stump: A competent solver nets the cancel and rebill lines, maps premises to counties, takes Pine Harbor's AMI accounts from their calendar-month bills, prorates every other bill's therms across the months it covers by days of service and files Ottercreek at $1,135,000 and Brennock at $2,465,000 (the region's January at 11,190,000 therms) against the golden $1,230,000 and $2,380,000, because use inside a bill follows the weather: the first eighteen days of January were milder than the December and February days billed with them and the 19 to 31 January cold snap colder, and day-proration treats every day of a bill as burning the same gas.

lineage.driver: A unit's months are counted where its return arrived and estimated where it did not, and its quarter is known complete from a second record that counts the same thing; the quarter's shortfall against that record is the estimate's error and sits in the month that was estimated, the unit's fullest, so spreading the shortfall over the quarter in proportion leaves the peak month short and only the estimated month takes it.
lineage.stump: A competent analyst fills the missing August returns at the stratum's occupancy, benchmarks each comune's July to September to its declared tourist-tax nights by spreading the shortfall over the three months in proportion, and designates the comuni that series puts over 30 nights a resident; the step that lands it there is spreading the gap, when the gap is the error of the filled August returns, and putting it all in August carries more comuni over the line.
